subject: Rack-by-rack cluster plan, topology constraints, and NVMe burst strategy
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Thomas Bell <tbell@crestline.ai>, ops@crestline.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-15 09:12 -0700
Subject: Rack-by-rack cluster plan, topology constraints, and NVMe burst strategy

Hi Thomas —

Thanks for walking us through the site photos this morning. I pulled together a short rack-by-rack checklist and a few follow-ups so we can lock down the cluster footprint and the storage fallback behavior before boarding the field crew. Attached: crestline-cluster-layout-v3.pdf and the NVMe failure-mode matrix.

Key open points we need to confirm from your side before our design freeze:
- Per-rack power: are the PDUs rated at 32A or 20A per phase? This affects node counts and redundant PSUs.
- Local NVMe: which chassis will have dual NVMe per node vs single? We need this to size local-ssd-backed pods and eviction tolerance.
- Fabric topology: confirm whether spine switches support BGP EVPN (preferred) or if we must rely on static layer-3 routes (we can work with either, affects MetalLB config).
- Egress constraints: does the site require NAT egress through a specific perimeter device (we saw an IPS at rack A3)? If so, we'll provide exact CIDR/port lists.

Proposed decisions we will implement unless you flag them:
- Node sizing: 3 node types (control {3x}, small worker w/1xNVMe, large worker w/2xNVMe for GPU inference).
- Storage: use hostPath ephemeral for checkpoint caching; persistent volumes via on-site SAN (iSCSI LUNs) exposed through CSI multipath driver for stateful workloads. Rook/Ceph is off the table for this initial launch due to storage team preference.
- PV binding: Use WaitForFirstConsumer to ensure proper topology-aware provisioning across racks.
- NVMe burst: our runtime will write large KV checkpoints to local NVMe, replicate to SAN nightly; on NVMe failure, nodes will be cordoned and workloads drained to SAN-backed pods.

Can you confirm PDUs and which racks will host the dual-NVMe chassis by end of day Monday? Also flag any procurement restrictions for the SAN LUNs (LUN naming, iqn allow-listing, firewall egress).

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Solutions Manager, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
From: Thomas Bell <tbell@crestline.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, ops@crestline.ai
Date: 2026-08-15 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Rack-by-rack cluster plan, topology constraints, and NVMe burst strategy

Hannah —

Thanks, got the docs. Quick answers: PDUs in racks A1-A6 are 32A (single phase), A7-A12 are 20A. Dual-NVMe chassis will be in racks A1, A2, A5, A6 — the rest are single-NVMe for now.

Fabric: switches are EVPN-capable but the network team wants us to stick to static L3 routing for the first rollout; they will enable EVPN only after the initial acceptance. Egress: yes, all outbound must traverse the perimeter NAT at rack A3 (IPS device). We'll provide the NAT egress IP and any ACLs by COB Monday.

SAN LUNs: storage team requires iqn and hostgroup mapping; they prefer us to request LUN numbers rather than carve our own. No Ceph for now as you noted.

If you can send the specific LUN naming template and the list of iSCSI initiator iqns you need, we'll queue it.

- Thomas
Crestline Robotics — Site Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Thomas Bell <tbell@crestline.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-16 08:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Rack-by-rack cluster plan, topology constraints, and NVMe burst strategy

Thomas —

Great, thanks for the clarity. Action items from our side:
1) Hannah/Irene: I will draft the PV class and CSI parameters to match iqn-based LUN map (expect a template today).
2) Irene: can you validate kubelet eviction thresholds for NVMe-backed pods? My recommendation: evictionHard: memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<5% with node-level watchdog to start crimson replication offload after sustained disk usage>75% for 3m.
3) Thomas: please send the NAT egress IP + allowed egress ports (we will restrict outbound to our update hosts and REDWOOD telemetry endpoints).

Design notes I will include in the doc: topology-aware storage provisioning (topology keys: rack, zone), MetalLB in layer-2 mode with static ARP proxies for the initial rollout, and a documented failover path: local NVMe -> SAN mount -> cross-rack standby nodes.

Also, small UX ask: for the nightly checkpoint sync to SAN we will need a 1Gbps sustained window between racks A1/A2 and the SAN head; if the SAN team can reserve that window between 02:00-04:00 local, it will keep replication windows small.

I'll attach the PV/SC templates shortly.

Marissa
Senior Deployment Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Thomas Bell <tbell@crestline.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17 15:43 -0700
Subject: Re: Rack-by-rack cluster plan, topology constraints, and NVMe burst strategy

Marissa/Team —

Quick verification from infra: proposed eviction thresholds look sane but we want a slightly more conservative default for initial rollout. Proposal (will lock unless Crestline objects):
- evictionHard: memory.available<150Mi,nodefs.available<3%
- evictionSoft: memory.available<250Mi (for 2m), nodefs.available<5% (for 3m)
- kube-reserved: cpu=200m,memory=1Gi; system-reserved: cpu=100m,memory=512Mi

I instrumented a small stress-run on a similar 1xNVMe node last week — when NVMe IO climbed >85% for >90s we saw pod eviction start but kubelet drain can take 30-90s depending on terminationGracePeriod. So:
- We'll implement a node watchdog that toggles the node.label nvme.burst=degraded and triggers the pod-disruption-budgets to allow quicker movement of critical pods to SAN-backed nodes.

I pushed PV/SC templates to the Drive folder (link above) and added CSI multipath config snippets for the storage team. Thomas — I left a sample iqn list and would prefer the storage team to return the LUN mapping CSV in the same Drive folder.

If no objections from Crestline by EOD tomorrow we will:
- Freeze cluster footprint and allocate provision tickets for LUN creation.
- Schedule a dry-run of node cordon/drain on a staging rack (A12) for next Tue.

Thanks,
Irene
Lead Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
